answer: A harness, in the context of AI agents, is the software that manages the model [1, 2]. It’s described as “what adds software that manages the model” [1]. Specifically, the harness assembles the model input from various sources such as system prompts, project instructions, and conversation data [2]. It then calls the model, validates its actions against defined parameters, executes tools, collects outputs, and adds them to the next model input [2]. The harness also manages things like state, logs, budgets, and stopping rules [2]. A helpful analogy is comparing the model to an engine of a car, with the harness providing all the other necessary components [1, 2].
